title: Per-request priority routing with version affinity and graceful fallback paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a deterministic, debuggable routing resolution that composes region selection, customer tier routing, per-request priority, and model-version affinity while providing graceful fallbacks to compatible model variants during capacity constraints or rollout failures. This ticket captures the API contract changes, resolution algorithm, and rollout strategy so product and infra can reason about semantics and tooling (logs, metrics, rollout controls).
design_summary: Proposal: Introduce a small, well-ordered priority function that produces an ordered candidate list for each request. Steps: 1) Evaluate hard constraints (region, tier, customer-specified version pin). 2) If version is pinned and available on chosen region/tier, route to pinned instance. 3) If pinned version is unavailable, construct a fallback chain using "compatibility tags" and a weighted cost heuristic (latency SLO delta + token-cost delta). 4) Apply rollout buckets (canary/A-B) as soft constraints: a request can be sampled into a rollout bucket only if candidate meets compatibility. 5) Respect sticky affinity for long-running sessions (cookie/connection-based) so canary exposures remain stable. 6) Provide deterministic tie-breakers (request id hash + seed) for repeatability in replay/simulations. The routing engine will surface the final decision provenance as a compact decision trace in logs and tracing spans.
implementation_plan: Schema: extend route config with 'compatibility_tags' and 'fallback_chain' metadata fields (config stored in config-service).

Routing engine: implement computeCandidateList(request) -> ordered candidates. Add scoring function that combines: region_match (binary), tier_score, version_affinity_score (high for pin), canary_bucket_score, cost_penalty, and health_penalty.
Affinity: implement request-affinity token that persists mapping user_id/session -> variant for sticky canary exposure with TTL and eviction policy.

Fallback engine: build a fallback resolution that prefers same-architecture models, then quantization-compatible variants, then lower-cost variants; include compatibility tags to avoid semantic regressions.
Config UI/Console: surface rollout weights, pin overrides, and an 'explain route' view showing decision trace for a sampled request.
Observability: add metrics for 'pinned->success' rate, 'pinned->fallback' rate, fallback-latency delta, canary-violation alerts, and a per-request decision_trace log field.
Testing: unit tests for scoring, chaos-testing with simulated region outages, and end-to-end traffic replay against shadow runtime.
Rollout: ship behind a feature flag; start with internal tenants, then graduated beta customers, then global rollout with monitoring gates.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic routing for a given request and config: given same seed and request attributes, decision_trace must be identical.
Pinned version semantics: requests with pinned version route to pinned variant when healthy; if not healthy, follow fallback chain and increment 'pinned->fallback' metric.
Canary exposure: canary weight respected within ±1% for sampled production traffic during steady-state, and sticky affinity maintains exposure for sessions across requests.
Performance: median extra latency added by routing decision path < 2ms on p95 request path and CPU/memory overhead within budget for routing service (target under 5% additional CPU).
Observability: Console shows per-route counts for pinned hits, pinned fallbacks, and top fallback targets for 30d window.
Safety: Rollout gates: if pinned->fallback rate or downstream latency regresses beyond thresholds, automatic rollback of rollout buckets occurs.
risks_mitigation: Cache fragmentation: affinity and per-request scoring can increase KV/cache churn. Mitigation: coalesce affinity buckets, introduce TTLs and aggregation heuristics in cache key generation.
Semantic regressions from fallback variants: require compatibility tags and a human-reviewed allowlist for unsafe degradations (e.g., changing tokenizer/semantics).
Operational complexity: provide a minimal 'safe-fallback' mode that only allows variants with identical contract; gradual opt-in for more aggressive fallbacks.
Data exposure: decision_trace may contain sensitive routing reasons; redact customer identifiers and store traces behind RBAC in console.
